title: Latency-tiered demultiplexing scheduler with kernel hinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode arbitration struggles to balance per-tenant latency SLOs and aggregate throughput when attention cost and kernel latency vary. We see 95th tail regressions on mixed workloads where short-chat prefill requests are delayed by long-step generation tasks and by suboptimal kernel choices for small sequence lengths.

Goal: Implement a latency-tiered demultiplexer (demux) scheduler that assigns incoming requests into latency tiers (fast, normal, background) and drives phase-splitting decisions plus kernel-hint signals to the kernel selection layer. The demux should: 1) enable fast-paths for short/interactive prefill+decode, 2) avoid starvation of background batches, and 3) emit stable latency/throughput tradeoff knobs for the control plane.

Approach:
- Classify requests at admission using cheap heuristics (prompt length, requested max tokens, model family, tenant SLA).
- Split phases more aggressively for fast-tier requests: allow microphase prefills and smaller decode slices to reduce tail latency at cost of marginal throughput.
- For background-tier traffic, coalesce phases and favor high-throughput kernels (larger matmul tiling, int8 paths).
- Surface a per-tenant soft-budget token-credit that the arbiter uses to avoid prolonged preemption of throughput traffic.
- Emit kernel hint metadata (e.g., prefer small-sequence specialized kernels, attention-sparsity route) to the kernel selection API so the runtime picks optimal kernels per microphase.
- Integrate with existing KV cache reuse logic and prefix caching to prevent duplication of work when a fast microphase follows a coalesced prefill.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce 95th latency for interactive workloads by >=20% in mixed workload simulation (equal mix short/long).
- Maintain <=5% throughput drop for background batch workloads vs baseline.
- No increase in error rate or dropped requests.
- Feature flag + rollout plan + metrics dashboards in place.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Over-splitting increases kernel scheduling overhead -> mitigate with adaptive coalescing thresholds.
- Kernel hinting adds interface surface; needs backward compatibility for older runtimes.
- Tenant soft-budgets may require calibration to avoid starvation or gaming.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation harness + microbench: validate heuristics.
2) Canary on dedicated pool with synthetic mixed traffic.
3) Gradual ramp to 20% production traffic with observability and revert gating.

Instrumentation & observability:
- New Grafana dashboard: demux-tier-latency, tiered-throughput, kernel-hint-match-rate.
- Trace labels for phase splits and kernel hints to correlate with tail latency.

Operational notes: leave default config conservative (favor throughput) and expose control-plane knobs: fast_tier_max_tokens, microphase_size, tenant_credit_window.
